_about: Pinned hashes and known gate failures. Machine-editable by --rebaseline. History in tests/BASELINE.md. READ THIS BEFORE CHASING A HASH: determinismHash and the smoke tables are CHANGE DETECTORS, not the determinism invariant. The invariant is that the same seed+tick+inputs reproduce bit-identically, and the determinism gate tests that separately (twice-run comparison) -- it keeps passing while these values move. All we require is determinism; new numbers are fine. An intentional change to hashed state (a reaction chance, a material, a sim.* value, a re-baked asset) ALWAYS moves them: run --selftest --rebaseline, commit the new values with the change, and move on. Do not investigate an expected move, do not try to restore the old number, and do not call it a broken sim. Only an UNEXPECTED move is a finding.

_treeAtlas_about: tree-atlas gate. treeAtlasHash is FNV-1a over the uploaded atlas buffer (assets/trees/*.svtree, remapped to engine material ids). It moves when a species is re-baked -- which also moves determinismHash, so this is what names WHICH asset did it instead of leaving a world-hash diff with no cause attached. Re-bake with node scripts/bake_trees.mjs, then --selftest --rebaseline.
_scale_about: scale gate. scaleMetres_<def> is that asset's size in METRES, recorded at 10 voxels/metre. These are the cross-scale pins: they are checked against a DIFFERENT kVoxelMeters than they were recorded at, which is the only thing that makes them non-circular (worldSize/skinScale*kVoxelMeters reduces algebraically to box/artVoxelsPerMetre and would agree with itself at any scale). Tolerance is 1.5 cells, since art is quantised and two scales may legitimately land on different whole cells. A move here means an asset changed physical size -- re-author or re-pin deliberately, do not rebaseline reflexively.

_solute_about: The solute layer (src/test/selftest_solute.cpp, docs/PLAN_solutes.md). _wound_about: The wound model (src/test/selftest_wound.cpp). THRESHOLDS, not observations: these are read by the gates, so retuning what counts as a chip or how many blows take an arm costs a JSON edit and no rebuild. woundAccumMin/MaxHits is a BAND on purpose -- the property is that a blade is neither instant (the old three-threshold behaviour, which lands at 1) nor asymptotic (a model that only ever chips, which never severs at all), and an exact count would pin the suite to one rig's arm thickness and one set of gore.cut* values. woundChipMaxFraction is what would have caught the old radial carve: it removed a sphere the size of the limb. woundHeftHeavy is the second arm of the heft differential, and it must stay well clear of 1.0 or 'strictly fewer hits' becomes a coin flip on rounding.
_woundAccumHeft_about: RETUNED 2026-09-19 after the owner's gore retune (b48fb4d: gore.cutLength 0.9 -> 0.64, gore.cutDepthPower 0.32 -> 0.15; melee.fullSpeedMps 3.4 -> 20 is what the in-game swing now ramps power against). A heft-1.0 kerf at the fixture's power 0.75 is 0.54 world voxels along the edge and the human thigh is ~0.75 across, so the slot advances through the limb without ever spanning it and neither structural rule in Mob::CarveLimb sees a disconnection: measured 46 of 46 hits at heft 1.0 with the limb still on (it took 5 before the retune), and 13 hits at heft 2.5 on the same limb, same cross-section, inset 230. woundAccumHeft is therefore the heft wound-accumulate hacks with -- the claim is that sustained cuts sever THROUGH Sever(), made with a kerf that can reach the far side -- and the band moved from 2..14 to 3..40 around the measured 13: 1-2 is the old instant sever, 40+ (cap woundAccumMaxHits*3+4 = 124) is a model that only grinds. wound-heft's light arm is still the sword at 1.0 and is allowed to NOT sever within the cap, which counts as more hits than any severed count. _headCleave_about: head-cleave (src/test/selftest_wound.cpp; phys/kerf.h KerfBite, 2026-09-25). THRESHOLDS, not observations. A blow parts a limb when its bite (chip area + gore.cleaveArea shaped by power) covers the whole plane it cuts within its edge, priced by material hardness over gear.cutHardnessRef. Measured on the human head: neck planes 1.25-1.28 world vox^2 from along 0.3 to 0.7 (0.1-0.2 is the 0.88 skin cap inside the collar; 0.8-0.9 the chin, 1.6-1.7), jaw 2.3-3.1, skull 2.7-5. headCleaveNeckFrom/To is the band B swings across: every plane in it must cleave at power 1 (sword budget 1.90 at cleaveArea 1.6) and none at headCleaveWeakPower (budget 0.80). headCleaveSkullRatio is how much dearer the skull must be. C chops a corpse with headCorpseJitter (+-4 cm on a 10 cm neck) of aim wander, POOLED over headCorpseRuns wanders because one run is a lottery (the ragged rim is keyed on the creature id: the same aim parted a neck in 9 chops at one fixture and 18 at another); the caps are on the MEAN. A groove-finding pull (the blade sliding into an old cut) was built and measured here and REMOVED: at +-2 cm it changed nothing (86 vs 87 chops over 6 wanders), at +-4 cm with a notch test 130 vs 142 (noise), and its only large effect came from mistaking the neck under the chin for a groove.

_woundChipStain_about: ARMING RADII for wound-chip's two blood claims (2026-09-19). Blood on a cut is two mechanisms: the SOAK rewrites exposed tissue within gore.woundStainRadius into the wound material, the SMEAR lays stain bits over everything within gore.stainCutRadius. The owner's retune took woundStainRadius 0.9 -> 0.1 (under one skin cell at skinScale 8, so a cut rewrites nothing: measured 0) and stainCutRadius 1.6 -> 0.4 (still tints the kerf walls). Each half is asserted only while its own radius, read off the live Tuning, reaches the arming value here -- so the rewrite claim re-arms by itself if the soak is turned back up. 0.5 world voxels is four skin cells at scale 8; 0.25 is two.
_impact_about: The other two kinds of blow (src/test/selftest_impact.cpp; game/impact.h). THRESHOLDS, not observations, exactly as the wound block above: a strike is three parts now, and these four gates own the BLUNT and the BITE while the wound gates own the CUT. impactBluntDentMaxFraction is a BAND and not a number, for the reason woundAccumMin/MaxHits is one -- the claim is that a mace dents (removes SOMETHING) without dismembering, and an exact figure would pin the suite to one rig's limb thickness. It sits above Mob::kLimbCollapseFraction's complement on purpose: the sever is REFUSED by Mob::BluntCarveScope rather than merely unreached, so a dent that passes the point a blast would have shed the limb is the interesting case rather than a failure. impactArmorSpread and impactFistSpread are how far the repeated blows WANDER, in world voxels: a radial dent saturates on one cell (the first blow empties the ball and every one after it finds that space gone -- the same failure the kerf's entry-plane snap exists to fix), and 24 gauntlet blows on one point measured 2 voxels, a true number about a thing nobody does. The same fixed sequence runs in both arms of each gate, so a comparison between profiles stays one. impactArmorBladeShellMaxFraction is what a blade does to plate over impactArmorHits blows -- gear.cutHardnessMin floors the kerf at one lattice cell, so ZERO is the wrong claim and a few per cent is the right one; the mace arm is asserted RELATIVE to it, not against a second constant, because the property is the difference. impactFistBlunt is the bare fist's trauma and lives here rather than in C++ because the real number arrives with package B's `natural` block on the mob sidecar and this gate should not need a rebuild on the day it does. impactFistIronPerHitFraction is bounded by woundChipMaxFraction above -- the wound gates' own figure for one sword cut -- which is what makes 'caving a face in SLOWLY' mean something rather than being a second free constant. biteRotHits/Hp size a zombie's mouthful; the gate asserts rotflesh > 0 on flesh and == 0 through a cuirass, and neither is a tunable number.
_impactPulp_about: The DISSOLUTION ARM of impact-blunt and impact-fist (2026-09-19, gore.pulpRotRate / bluntCarveRadius / pulpCarveFrom, commit 54ba62b). A blunt dent is no longer carved by the blow that earns it: Mob::BluntHit flags the limb and Mob::BluntPulpTick eats the pulped (blood >= gore.pulpAmt) voxels one at a time over the ticks that follow, so both gates read the limb the instant the blows end (that count must be UNCHANGED -- nothing leaves in the swing) and again after ticking it with gore.pulpRotRate cranked to impactPulpRot for impactPulpTicks ticks, blood loss off. These two are the arm, not the claim, exactly as jointRotRate is: the shipped 1.5 vox/min makes a thigh's crater a minute of sim. 30 vox/min on a skinScale-8 limb is ~8 lattice voxels a tick, so the 117 pulped cells impact-blunt measured are gone inside 60 ticks; on a scale-4 rig it is ~1 a tick and 60 ticks still shows the dent. What is asserted is DIRECTION and the band: the mace's limb lost > 0 and <= impactBluntDentMaxFraction and stayed on; the gauntlet's lost > 0 and slowly; the bare fist (bluntCarve 0, never flagged) lost nothing through the same ticks.
_biteInfect_about: bite-infect drives Mob::InfectTick (gore.infectSpreadRate / infectRotRate). SINCE 2026-10-01 the rates are PER VOXEL PER SECOND (0.04 / 0.02 here, R = 2; the shipped rot is 0.00075 / 0.000375) and the limb is read with tombstones excluded (a per-voxel eat flushes in batches); the text below is the per-limb history. These three are the ARM, not the claim: the gate asserts only DIRECTION -- the rot grows, voxels leave, and neither happens in the rates-0 control arm -- because how MUCH is a tuning question and pinning it would make every retune a gate failure. They are cranked far above the shipped 1.0/0.5 vox/min so the window is seconds instead of minutes, and biteInfectRot is bounded from above on purpose: 2.0 over 300 ticks eats ~12% of a thigh, comfortably under Mob::kLimbCollapseFraction, and a fixture that severs before it is read reports a correct measurement of nothing. biteInfectMaxStep is the one row that is a CLAIM rather than an arm: the most rot the limb may gain on any SINGLE tick. At biteInfectSpread the pass owes ~1.7 lattice voxels a tick, so an honest per-tick draw can hand over only 1 or 2 and 4 is headroom. It exists because the first shipped version banked the fraction and spent it in bursts of ~32 -- same average, every other assertion here green, and the rot visibly advancing in slabs. Only the STEP separates a rate realised by chance from a rate realised in instalments.
_venomWound_about: venom-wound (PLAN_weapon_coats B, DESIGN.md 'Infection is a material'). TimeScale is the ARM: the gate hands MobSystem a copy of materials.json with envenomed's spread AND eat both multiplied by it, so the window is seconds instead of minutes and the eat/spread ratio -- the claim -- is untouched. Radius is the hole carved on the outside of each of four limbs (world voxels) before the venom soak. The CLAIMS: EatRatioLo..Hi is the band round 3 for eaten / seeded summed over the eight arm and leg segments (R = 2/3 gives 3 D eaten per D seeded for a well-mixed process; a wound's 2-cell-thick soft-tissue shell runs out of neighbours and pulls the mean under 3 -- measured 2.50, 2.55 and 1.74 on four limbs -- and the offspring variance R/(1-R)^3 = 18 a seed makes the sum noisy, hence 1.5..4.5); RotCrank multiplies gore.infectMobMult for the rot + venom arm; WindowLo..Hi bounds the measured burn-out (the LAST of four limbs to clear, plus any limb a joint crossing re-seeded) against the branching-process mean H(D, R) / mu for the largest single-limb dose (DESIGN.md 'Infection is a material'). BoneLossMax: A's bone census loss minus the control's (same pits, no venom). rotClock*: the rot-clock ruler (crank on gore.infectMobMult, give-up). Each limb's burn-out is a random walk whose sd is about 0.7x its mean at a 10-cell dose, so the last of four lands well above 1: measured 2.96 (866 ticks against 293) on 2026-10-01, hence 4.5. MaxTicks is the give-up.

_burnCapFireTicks_about: burn-cap arm C: the most ticks the bonfire may take to kill (the loop ends at the death). 1200 had no margin left by 2026-10-01 (deaths at 1152 and 1184, one survivor at 66.0% burnt) once the fire column also reached the feet; 2400 is the ceiling, the claim (it dies of the burn cap, at or past the death knot) is unchanged.
_jointRot_about: SINCE 2026-10-01: per-voxel rates (0.6 / 0.3 per voxel per second, R = 2), the teeth go into the arm's PARENT at its SOCKET (MobSystem::LimbSocketWorld; the root was not every limb's parent, and an arm's socket used to measure EMPTY so the parent-side test never ran), a bite jointRotBiteScale x the shipped radius, and bleeding is not hp in the fixture (both arms used to bleed out first). Measured: off at tick 52 alive, control held to its death at 238. joint-rot drives the JOINT ATTACHMENT rule (Mob::JointAttached, reached from Mob::CarveLimb and Mob::DropDisconnectedChildren). The first three rows are the ARM, not the claim: the rates are cranked far above the shipped 1.0/0.5 vox/min so the window is seconds, and 600 ticks is long enough for the CONTROL arm to reach the old whole-limb collapse rule, which is what lets the two be told apart. jointRotFracMin is the one row that is a CLAIM: how much of itself the limb must still have when it leaves, for the sever to be a statement about the JOINT rather than about the volume. Measured 2026-09-19 -- the teeth go into the TORSO at the hip and arm A took the leg at tick 49 with 95% of it left (nothing ever touched the leg; the socket was eaten out from the torso side), while the control with gore.woundNeckRadius = 0 held it to tick 338 and 28%, which is kLimbCollapseFraction doing its old job. 50% sits between them with room on both sides.
_bodyStain_about: THRESHOLDS for the `body-stain` gate (DESIGN.md section 7, Blood on a body). bodyStainBoneMinFraction: of the bone voxels a deep kerf exposes, at least this fraction must carry a stain (bone is always shown bloodied to some degree; the soak floors it at gore.stainBoneMin). bodyStainWashMaxFraction: after 60 ticks in a box of water, the root limb may keep at most this fraction of the stained voxels it had after 30 ticks in a box of blood. bodyStainShallowMaxRise: standing 30 ticks in a two-voxel-deep pool, no limb voxel more than this many world voxels above the pool's top may carry a stain (the contact pass dilates a liquid cell by one voxel; blood on the thigh from an ankle-deep pool is the 2026-09-13 owner report).
_bodyCoat_about: THRESHOLDS for the `body-coat` gate (P1 of the body-coat scaffolding). A coat is a SUBSTANCE on a body voxel — a material id plus an amount — so these bound how it behaves as one. bodyCoatHoldMinFraction: over 150 ticks at the authored drying rate (blood: coat.decay 20 s per amount level, i.e. a 600-tick period) the cut limb must keep at least this fraction of the voxels its cut stained. bodyCoatDecayMaxFraction: with coat.decayScale set so that period becomes two ticks, the same count must fall to at most this fraction within the gate's 400-tick cap. COUNTS ARE OF VOXELS ABOVE THE MATERIAL'S OWN coat.decayFloor (2026-09-19): blood authors decayFloor 1 since 28ebf8d (2026-09-16) and Mob::StainTick never takes a voxel under it, so a count at amount >= 1 could not fall and the decay arm read 43 -> 43 with every voxel correctly parked at the residual. The gate reads the floor off the material; the fractions are unchanged.
_heal_about: THRESHOLDS for heal-restore (part B, a heavy crater wound soaked in enchanted blood) and heal-wound (a cut + ~1600 cooked cells doused in it). Enchanted blood heals at coat.restoreRate 0.1 world voxels a second (~51 skin cells/s on a human) so a heavy wound knits over ~30 s (owner, 2026-09-27). Fractions are of the wound's missing + changed recipe cells at the start. heal.minLeftAt5s: at least this much is still unhealed after 150 ticks (it is NOT instant). heal.maxLeftAt35s: at most this much is left after 1050 ticks (it DOES finish in about half a minute). heal.minScatterRank: the first 20% of cells to grow back, ranked by distance to the joint among all that grew (0 nearest, 1 farthest), must average at least this -- a smooth front from the joint reads ~0.1, uniform noise ~0.5. heal.minHeavyWoundCells: fixture sanity, the heavy wound must be at least this big. heal.repourTicks: both gates pour enchanted blood again every this many ticks until the limb is whole -- one application dries off in ~20 s (coat.decay 1.2, owner 2026-09-27), so a heavy wound takes repeated pours.
_ragdoll_about: THRESHOLDS for the `ragdoll` gate. A dummy knocked down by the X-detonate charge 6 voxels away must move its pelvis between min and max voxels in 1.5 s (min proves it flew, max proves it did not leave the county), and must be back on its feet within getUpMaxTicks.
_ragdoll_repeat_about: The fastest LIMB (m/s) of a wizard put through main.cpp's whole explosion block, standing and then again while already limp: ragdoll.maxLaunchSpeed (14) plus the fall it picks up. Before the rig skip list a limp hand took the per-body debris impulse (impulse / 0.3 kg) and the launch on top.
_ragdoll_burn_about: The player avatar on fire in stock cloth with the capsule proxy present: PlayerPushOut per tick (voxels) and total displacement over 400 ticks. Before the per-body-max + mass floor in PlayerPushOut: 62 vox in one tick, 432 vox before death.
_ragdoll_spin_about: The TUMBLE (ragdoll.blastLimbBias / blastSpinGain): the same charge at the ankles and then over the head, the same distance from the pelvis either way, must spin the rig in OPPOSITE directions about z by at least MinSpin rad/s and tip its pelvis's up axis by at least MinTiltGap between the two arms 12 ticks later. MaxLimbSpeedRatio holds the differential to a lean: no limb may leave the blast that many times faster than the slowest. Observed 2026-09-11 at bias 0.35 / gain 0.65: +0.61 and -0.54 rad/s, spread 1.12x / 1.18x, tilt gap 1.19.
_corpseArmor_about: THRESHOLDS for the `corpse-armor` gate (owner report 2026-09-13: an armoured NPC whose head had been cut off spasmed, flew apart while still jointed, and froze the game for minutes). The gate dresses the fixture in everything assets/items ships, cuts off the severable limb carrying the most armour, kills it, and watches the corpse for 3 s. MaxSpeedVox and MaxSpreadVox bound how fast and how far the remains travel. MaxPeggedTicks is the real claim: body-ticks spent at 90% of Jolt's own angular clamp. The PEAK spin is deliberately not bounded -- a limb thrown by a killing blow may touch 47.12 rad/s for a tick, and an assertion would have to sit above the clamp to pass at all -- but a limb that SITS there is being driven by its own constraints, which is the bug. Observed 2026-09-13 with the runaway net in: 69.1 vox/s, 34.5 vox, 1 pegged body-tick, net damped 0 / cut 0 / repaired 0, worst step 2.4 ms.
_corpseArmorPegged_about: SPLIT BY TIME 2026-09-19. The pegged count was one bucket, so the corpse LANDING and the corpse being DRIVEN read as the same number. Measured after the owner's gore retune, with the corpse coming down whole (hand.L under its gauntlet is no longer cut through in 120 strokes since 89b4bb9 retargets a probe under a worn shell onto the shell): 7 body-ticks across 5 bodies, the last on tick 15 and none after -- the kill's own transient, the case _corpseArmor_about already exempts for the PEAK. corpseArmorSettleTicks is where the split falls; corpseArmorMaxPeggedTicksEarly caps the first bucket loosely (a motor pegs every body every tick and a 27-body corpse blows through 20 in a single tick); corpseArmorMaxPeggedTicks keeps its tight cap on everything after, which is where the report lives.
_corpseSleep_about: THRESHOLDS for the `corpse-sleep` gate (docs/PLAN_corpse_is_a_mob.md: a corpse is a dead Mob and keeps its rig, so a settled one must cost nothing), at the AUTHORED drying rates since P2d. corpseSleepMaxTicks: how long a dressed, blood-soaked corpse killed without a wound may take to fall asleep -- Jolt sleeping the ragdoll, its anatomy blood voxels decaying out (site-dependent, 0 to ~700 ticks), plus MobSystem::kDeadSleepTicks of every criterion quiet. The blood COAT they leave dries at 20 s a level for ~15,000 ticks and no longer holds it awake (MobSystem::CoatDriesAsleep). corpseSleepWindow: how long it is then watched asleep, over which it must run no dead PostStep and register terrain anchors only on its keep-alive stride. corpseSleepDryTicks: the whole run, long enough for at least one 600-tick blood period after it sleeps; over it the sleeping corpse must never wake, must take a drying visit, and on every tick it slept through the awake stain pass run as a shadow (MobSystem::ShadowStainTick) must write nothing -- so sleeping skipped only no-op ticks and the coat is what continuous drying leaves. The corpse is SOAKED in blood (every limb, amount 6) after the kill so the coat is there on any site, and lies on the first candidate site with no liquid within 12 voxels on the CPU mirror (470, the old site, is a pond's shore; a ragdoll rolling into it is wet, in contact and correctly awake). Measured 2026-09-24 in a --verify list: site 510, asleep at 69 with a 179,004 blood coat on it that P1's rule held awake, 0 wakes, 2 visits (179,004 -> 147,467), 0 of 1,428 shadow ticks wrote. At site 470 the anatomy blood decaying out of the torso (burn pass, not the coat) took 742 ticks.
_corpseCap_about: The `corpse-cap` gate: kill MobSystem::kMaxDeadMobs + corpseCapExtra creatures in order and run one tick; the dead must be within their own caps, the extra ones must be the OLDEST and must have decayed to loose dead flesh, and the living cap must still admit exactly kMaxMobs beside them.
_corpseSave_about: The `corpse-save` gate (PLAN_corpse_is_a_mob.md P2a, MOBS v6). corpseSavePoseTolVox: how far any limb of a loaded or unparked corpse may sit from where it lay when it was written (the record carries every limb's transform and a dead record is always placed, so this is float noise, not settling). corpseSaveMaxSettleVox: how far the root may then move over 30 stepped ticks -- a corpse wrongly stood up in Spawn's rest pose falls about its own height. The gate records corpseSavePoseVox, corpseSaveUnparkPoseVox and corpseSaveSettleVox.
_debrisGhost_about: gate debris-ghost (M9.4-C): a body owned by another player is a kinematic ghost that authors nothing. trackSlackVox is slack ON TOP OF one step of the fed velocity (a kinematic body is placed on the pose AND given its velocity, so it is measured one tick ahead by design -- measured 0.0224 vox against a 0.67 vox/s stream at 1/30 s). handoffTolVox allows for Jolt normalising a quaternion across the owned->ghost->owned round trip; the honest number is 0.
_ragdollDress_about: THRESHOLDS for the `ragdoll-dress` gate (owner report 2026-09-13: a clothed human going limp mid-fall 'becomes a crazy tangled mess ball of limbs and clothes that aren't actually connected properly'). A dressed human is made limp 200 voxels up and dropped under Jolt, then again on the spot at 30 m/s. ShellDrift/ShellTwist are how far a garment moves in the frame of the limb it is strapped to, and they are a CONSTANCY claim, not a smallness one: a worn shell is a kinematic follower with no constraint (MobLimb::wornHost), so its offset is derived and cannot change. LimbStretch is a joint's anchor measured in its PARENT's frame -- the point a ball joint welds -- so it catches a rig torn open by the anti-tunnel clamp without objecting to a limb that is merely rotating. Observed 2026-09-13: drift 0.000 / twist 0.06 deg / stretch 2.47 vox at 21.9 m/s. The SAME fixture with SANDVOX_NO_RIGWELD=1 (the A/B arm: jointed dynamic shells + the per-body clamp) gives drift 3.300, twist 151.50 deg and stretch 8.15 -- a greave rotated 151 degrees off the leg wearing it, which is the report in one number. The residual 2.4 vox of stretch is the solver's own softness at the landing impact and is the same in both arms of the new code.
_snapshotLatency_about: THRESHOLDS for the `snapshot-latency` gate (docs/PLAN_multiplayer_now.md N1). snapshotLatencyK is K -- World::kSnapshotLatency, the FIXED age of World::Snap(): a decision at tick T reads the world at T-K on every machine and at every frame rate. Pinned here so a change to K is visible as a gate line and not only as a moved world hash; K must stay <= SubmitTick's kPagedSnapshotMaxGap, because the page-table mirror dilates one N26 ring per tick of that gap. snapshotDrainedMaxWaits is the wait budget for the DRAINED arm, where every submit has provably retired before the next tick is encoded -- a wait there is a pipeline bug, not a slow GPU, so the budget is 0. The DEEP-QUEUE arm is reported and never asserted: a headless loop needs the snapshot from K ticks ago with no frame of real work in between and blocks by construction. The game's wait budget is measured with --frames 600 --autofly-surface, not by this gate.
_chunkHash_about: THRESHOLDS for the `chunk-hash` gate (docs/PLAN_multiplayer_m9.md M9.3-A). The per-chunk digest is a SECOND accumulator in sim_occupancy.wgsl's full entry point, keyed on the chunk-local cell index instead of the slot-global one, so it is a pure function of a chunk's 4,096 words -- which is what lets two machines ask 'is your copy of world chunk C the same as mine?' without shipping 16 KiB. chunkHashSettleTicks is how long each twice-run arm simulates before the tables are compared; chunkHashQuietCap bounds the quiesce loop that follows, so 'exactly one slot changed' is measured against a still background and not against a settling one. chunkHashChangedSlots is the measurement itself: one cell's palette nibble flipped, one slot's digest moved. It is 1 BY CONSTRUCTION and a 2 here means a digest is keyed on something it should not be -- it is not a number to re-pin when it moves.
_chunkResync_about: OBSERVED values for the `chunk-resync` gate (docs/PLAN_multiplayer_m9.md M9.3-C). Both are INFORMATIONAL and neither fails the gate: the gate's real claims are self-comparisons between two arms of the same scene (the repaired arm's world hash must EQUAL the control's, and the replay's must equal the recorded run's), which need no pin. chunkResyncSolidPct is how much of the subject chunk is non-air -- the gate refuses below 90% on its own, because a resync fixture that stopped being buried matter would be testing a quiet AIR chunk, which is not the case the repair is for. chunkResyncFrames is the framed record's tick count, which is a constant of the scene and moves only when the scene does.
_repose_about: repose gate (src/test/selftest_ca.cpp). THRESHOLDS, not observations: the runRiseMin/Max_* keys are read by the gate, so retuning what counts as a 2:1 or a 1:2 pile costs a JSON edit and no rebuild. run:rise is the pile's Manhattan reach over its peak height, so the ideal values are 3.0 / 2.0 / 1.0 / 0.5 for the four pure tiers -- the bands are wide because a 400-grain pile quantises hard (a peak of 4 vs 5 moves the ratio 25%) and because the apex starts as a 5x5 plateau rather than a point. The blend30/blend40 arms use REAL LOADER OUTPUT (PackRepose) and are the only arms that execute the per-grain blend hash at all; the gate asserts they differ from each other and sit between the pure tiers they mix, which is what catches a blend that has gone inert. The ORDERING is asserted separately and is the property that must not flap. awakeChunksMax is 0 on purpose: a lateral slide is the one powder move that does not lower a grain, so a nonzero count here means the termination argument in sim_step.wgsl's ANGLE OF REPOSE block is wrong, which is a rule-2 bug and not a threshold to raise. runRiseObserved_* are written by --rebaseline and read by nobody.
_opsReplay_about: The `ops-replay` gate (docs/PLAN_multiplayer_now.md N3). opsReplayBytes is INFORMATIONAL and does not fail the gate: it is the size of the framed op record for the 200-tick scene, and it moves whenever TickParams grows a word -- which is a change worth noticing (the record carries the whole struct, so every field added is 200 x 4 bytes here) but is not a correctness property. It moved +800 B (200 frames x 4) at M9.3-C, which is the chunkReplaces count kRecordVersion 3 appends to every frame. The gate's real claims are the 14 reproduced hash probes and the contested-cell probe, and neither is pinned in this file because both are self-comparisons.
_tickInput_about: The `tick-input` gate (docs/PLAN_multiplayer_now.md N2). endX/endY/endZ are the player's position after the gate's 300 scripted ticks, and endTolVox is how far it may move before the gate says so. They are a PIN, not an invariant: the gate's real claim is that arm A (1 tick per frame) and arm B (4 ticks per frame) produce a bit-identical trajectory and a bit-identical command stream, which is a self-comparison and is not pinned here. A player.* tuning edit legitimately moves the end position -- the gate marks that case pinned-only, so --selftest --rebaseline records it in one step.
_viewSmooth_about: The `view-smooth` gate. Bounds on the RENDER path only -- no sim value is involved, so these are thresholds rather than pins and moving one is a statement about how smooth the camera is allowed to stop being. maxFrameJumpVox: the largest single-FRAME change in drawn eye height while walking up a 1-voxel-per-4 staircase; the riser is 1.0 vox, so anything approaching that is the 30 Hz sawtooth the gate was written for. maxFrameDipVox: how far the eye may go DOWN on a frame while the body is climbing (the specific signature of the offset and the tick lerp double-counting a step). maxGapDriftVox: how far the drawn BODY may drift from the drawn EYE -- they get identical corrections, so the only correct value is ~0.
_net_about: The `net-loopback` gate (docs/PLAN_multiplayer_m9.md M9.2 package A; src/net/*). These are COVERAGE COUNTS, not thresholds and not physics: loopbackMsgs is how many framed messages crossed the in-memory Link pair, tcpMsgs how many crossed a real 127.0.0.1 socket in-process, helloFields how many fields of the handshake were perturbed one at a time and correctly named by Hello::FirstMismatch. They are pinned so that a subtest which silently SHRANK -- a script that stopped generating 70 KiB messages, a Hello field that stopped being compared because it was added to the struct and not to kHelloU32 -- shows up as a moved number instead of as a still-green gate. The gate's real claims (byte-exact in-order reassembly across partial reads, the refusal naming the right field in the right order, and the pacer never running a tick whose batch has not arrived) are self-comparisons and are NOT pinned here. helloFields moves when a field is added to Hello, which is a deliberate protocol change: --selftest --rebaseline records it. tcpMsgs is asserted ONLY when the socket arm actually came up -- the plan's kill criterion makes a firewall-blocked loopback listen advisory, since the in-memory pair covers the framing and the two-process smoke covers the socket.
_authority_about: The `authority` gate (docs/PLAN_multiplayer_m9.md M9.4 package A; src/net/authority.*). One COVERAGE COUNT and nothing else: authorityRows is how many truth-table rows the gate checked. Every row is a self-comparison -- it asserts a named claim about ownership (nearest-wins, resident-beats-near per protocol review finding 6, tie -> lower id, nobody, disconnect, hysteresis hold/release/eviction, per-entity memory, the feet floor, Comparable, and Owns for every Producer in an owned and a foreign chunk) and prints the claim that stopped being true. Those are not pinned here because they are right or wrong on their own terms, not relative to yesterday. The COUNT is pinned so that a deleted row or a loop that stopped running shows up as a moved number rather than as a still-green gate measuring less than it did. It moves when a row is ADDED (record it with --selftest --rebaseline) and when a Producer is added to sim/oprecord.h, since the Owns table covers all of them and asserts that it does.
_opsExchange_about: The `ops-exchange` gate (docs/PLAN_multiplayer_m9.md M9.3 package B; src/net/opsync.*). Two COVERAGE numbers and no thresholds. opsExchangeRows is how many named claims the gate checked: the wire blob's round trip and its refusal of a truncated or wrong-version payload, the copied slot->chunk arithmetic against World's own, the residency filter on a peer whose window is four chunks along (kept 8, dropped 8, and the drop names its chunk), the byte-for-byte equality of the merged batch between the HOST's seat and the CLIENT's over 200 ticks, the equal hash series that follows from it, author-major order read off the one tick both players author a brush op on, the D-tick delay warm-up, and the record of the host seat replaying to the same hashes. Every one of those is a self-comparison and is right or wrong on its own terms, so none of them is pinned; the COUNT is, so that a deleted row or a loop that stopped running is a moved number rather than a still-green gate measuring less. opsExchangeMergedMax is INFORMATIONAL (the largest single tick's merged op count) and exists so a failure can say which way the fixture moved rather than only that it did. Both move when the SCRIPT moves, which is a deliberate edit: --selftest --rebaseline records it.
_storeSync_about: The `store-sync` gate (docs/PLAN_multiplayer_m9.md M9.5 package B; src/net/storesync.*). ONE COVERAGE COUNT and nothing else. storeSyncRows is how many named claims the gate checked: the client's eviction landing in the host's store with its tick tag and leaving the unacked list, an older ChunkPut being refused AND still acked (an unacked stale put would be re-offered on every reconnect forever), a non-authority eviction sending nothing while an eviction of a chunk nobody else holds does send, the manifest -> Wanted -> ChunkGet -> ChunkData -> deliver path compared on BYTES rather than counted, a chunk in no manifest not being wanted, a ChunkMiss arriving as a message instead of as silence, a disconnect missing every outstanding request, an unacked put surviving a drop and being re-offered on reconnect, and meta.svm's SVM5 tick/seed pair round-tripping while a demoted SVM4 file still loads and reports the pair as UNKNOWN rather than as zero. Every one of those is a self-comparison and is right or wrong on its own terms, so none is pinned; the COUNT is, so that a deleted row or a loop that stopped running is a moved number rather than a still-green gate measuring less. It moves when a row is ADDED, which is a deliberate edit: --selftest --rebaseline records it. The gate never touches the world hash -- its SaveWorld/LoadWorld pair restores the grid it found and regenerates at the origin on the way out.
_twoPlayers_about: The `two-players` gate (docs/PLAN_multiplayer_m9.md M9.1 P3). Two scripted players 12 chunks apart in one world: player 0 collides through the snapshot mirror (World::KindAt, the mirror centred on it) and player 1 through World::KindAtCached plus PlayerSession::PrefetchAround, because the 3x3x3 mirror only ever covers ONE player and a body outside it reads Unknown -- which the controller treats as air, so KnownDrop clamps the descent and the body HOVERS rather than falls. p0End*/p1End* are PINS (endTolVox is the slack); a player.* tuning edit or a worldgen change legitimately moves them and the gate marks that case pinned-only so --rebaseline records it in one step. fallbackSettledBy is a THRESHOLD, not an observation: the tick by which player 1 must have stopped answering from the analytic TerrainHeight column and started answering from fetched voxels. A fetch lands 1-2 ticks plus World::kSnapshotLatency after it is asked for, so 60 is generous by an order of magnitude and a value that starts creeping is the fetch FIFO backing up. lastFallbackTick / fallbackAnswers / cacheAnswers / fetchRequests / fetchCoalesced are INFORMATIONAL -- nothing reads them; they exist so a failure says which way the fixture moved (CLAUDE.md rule 6). The gate's one non-rebaselinable claim is the twice-run hash sequence, which is a self-comparison and is not pinned here.
_remoteGhost_about: The `remote-ghost` gate (docs/PLAN_multiplayer_m9.md M9.2 package B). One local player plus one GHOST -- a peer's body fed a scripted PlayerState stream (game/remoteplayer.h) and never re-simulated, because no TickInput crosses the wire in the model of record: the peer is authoritative for its own controller and sends the OUTCOME. The gate calls the same four free functions session.cpp's phases B/H/I/O call, so it measures the code the game runs rather than a copy of it. posTolVox is a THRESHOLD, not an observation: how far the rig's root may sit from the state's pos, in voxels, on the worst tick of 300. The rig is placed from pos directly, so the only slack is the box reconstruction's rounding and a value that starts creeping means the ghost is being moved by something local -- a solver, a push-out, a ragdoll follow -- which is precisely what RemotePlayersPostStep refuses to do. spawnTick / worstPosErrVox / discardedOps / firstDiscardTick / leakedOps are INFORMATIONAL, recorded so a failure says which way the fixture moved (CLAUDE.md rule 6); leakedOps is the interesting one and it must be 0 -- a ghost authors NOTHING, because its owner is authoring the same ops on its own machine and applying them twice would diverge the two worlds on the first footstep. discardedOps being non-zero is the other half of that claim and is what stops it being a fixture that cannot fail. The gate's one non-rebaselinable claim is the twice-run hash sequence, a self-comparison, not pinned here.
_cactus-fell_about: Added 2026-09-12 and PASSING since the same day. A saguaro-sized fixture (40 tall, one arm, on a sand bed) severed 8 cells up, in three arms: the game's own path (GPU support flag only, no forced mirror fetches), the brush's CPU door plus forced fetches, and a stone-pad control. The assertion that was red for a day is game-arm-body-falls: the severed top became a 1184-voxel body within three ticks and then stood in the air (fell 0.5 cells in 300 ticks) because ManageTerrain meshed the collider around it from a mirror copy that still held the top and only re-fetched a chunk while dirty and 8 ticks after the last request. The debris system now reads its own not-yet-mirrored writes through a per-chunk overlay (NoteGridWrite / pendingVacate_) in both the flood and the collider build; the game-arm body falls ~11 cells on its own. cactusFell.minDropCells is the floor on that fall.
_debris_about: KNOWN-FAILING since the tree overhaul (2026-08-29), and the cause is understood: the gate drops 54 rigid bodies into open forest at x 40-125 / z 420-490, and trees now have real branch structure, so bodies get CAUGHT IN CANOPIES instead of reaching the ground. Confirmed by voxel dump -- a 1,752-voxel body hung at y=221 with ground at y=199 and an autumn-birch canopy at y=231. Nothing about the tree code is wrong; the fixture assumed open ground. Two honest fixes are open: make foliage not support rigid bodies (physically right, a behaviour change in src/phys/debris.cpp), or move the drop zone somewhere trees do not grow (cheaper, but then nothing exercises debris landing in a forest).
_gas_about: THE WINDOW EDGE AS A SINK (docs/PLAN_gas_particles.md stage 1). THRESHOLDS, not observations -- the gates read every one of these, so retuning what counts as a sheet or how long a parcel gets to cross a face costs a JSON edit and no rebuild. gasLeaveSheetMax is the whole point of the change: before it, a gas voxel at the window's top face could not tell 'out of the world' from a solid wall and sheeted across the ENTIRE top chunk plane (up to 1,024 chunks) until it decayed. 8 is 'the plume's own footprint and nothing more'. There is NO pre-change control number for it on this tree and there cannot be one from a gate -- the old behaviour does not exist in this binary -- so the gate prints what it measured beside the bound rather than claiming a delta. gasLeaveProbeTick is where the two synchronous probes (the outer density box, the parcel page walk) are taken; it is a SEGMENT BOUNDARY in the run, not a read inside the tick loop. gasReenterMinLanded is 128 of 256 -- half, measured at 251 -- and not 256 on purpose: parcels die of their authored decay on the way across, so an exact count would re-pin this gate to reactions.json. gasReenterTicks is the WHOLE run and not just a deadline: the smoke a landing makes is a rising gas voxel like any other, and 60 ticks later it has climbed out of the census box and reached the window's own ceiling, where it correctly becomes a parcel again -- which read as '0 smoke voxels, 83 parcels alive' and had nothing to do with re-entry. Measure where the subject is.
_gasFarPlume_about: FAR FIRE PLUMES (world.h kGasFarEmitMax, sim_gas.wgsl gasFarPlume). Thresholds, not observations. gasFarPlumeTicks is short on purpose: the plume is SYNTHESIZED FRESH every tick from a stateless hash, so there is nothing to converge and a longer run would only measure the same tick twelve more times -- what the ticks buy is the one-tick latency of the emitter upload and a few frames of the rising animation. gasFarPlumeMinCellMax and gasFarPlumeMinColumnSum are floors on the density the box holds over the frozen fire's own column, in the box's own 16-bit cell units (the renderer divides a cell by 512 to get a volume fraction, so 40 is about 8% of a solid cell and 2000 over the whole column is a plume you can see). They are FLOORS rather than pins because the shape is hash-scattered: pinning an exact sum would re-pin this gate to the puff hash and fail on any retuning of FAR_PLUME_DENSITY, which is a look constant. The claims that cannot be retuned away carry no number here and are the ones that matter: the control column must be exactly 0, the no-emitter arm must be exactly 0, the world hash must be IDENTICAL between the plume and no-plume arms (render-only means render-only), and the off arm's box must be byte-identical to the on arm's, which is how 'no gas row was recorded' is OBSERVED rather than argued.
_gasFarPlume2_about: THE LONG-RANGE BOX (world.h kGasFarOuterN). gasFarPlume2ChunksOut puts the frozen fire 128 chunks = 204.8 m from the window, which is half the long-range box's reach: comfortably past the near box at 51.2 m and comfortably inside the far one, so neither bound is what the gate measures. The two density floors are lower than the near gate's because a 6.4 m cell is one eighth the linear resolution: the wide plume is DENSER per cell (measured max 125 of 512, i.e. a quarter of a solid 6.4 m cell) but occupies far fewer of them, so the column SUM is about a tenth of the near gate's while the plume it draws is much larger in the frame; like the near gate's they are FLOORS on a hash-scattered shape, not pins. The claims with no number here are again the ones that matter: the control column is exactly 0, the NEAR box over the same site is exactly 0 (the two emitter lists are disjoint, which is what makes double-brightening impossible by construction rather than by a blend weight), the world hash is IDENTICAL with the wide list empty, and at render.farPlumeRange 0 the box is byte-identical four ticks later.
_gasFarPlume2Sparse_about: ARM E, the TREE-SIZED fire. Every other arm in this gate paints a WHOLE chunk of ember (~4,000 hot voxels, four saturated columns), and the wide splat scales its mass LINEARLY with the columns it aggregates -- so the whole-chunk fixture sat far above the renderer's erosion threshold while a real burning tree sat under it and was carved to nothing. That is the reported bug where only the biggest fire smokes at distance, and no arm could see it, because gasErode is a RENDER-side function and every gate here reads the density box. gasFarPlume2SparseDiv 16 keeps one hot voxel in sixteen (~255 total), which is tree-scale. THE FLOOR IS NOT A LOOK TARGET: with raymarch's GAS_CORE_COUNT_WIDE now derived from the same FILL/CHORD the wide deposit divides by, a peak of 5 against a wide core of 9.6 is s = 0.52, which is the SAME shape value the fine box gives this fire (peak ~27 against 51.2). The two boxes agreeing on how eroded a given fire is, is the whole point. Measured 4 -- it was 5 before FAR_PLUME_WIDE_HMIN let the plume SIZE scale below one full column, and the per-puff mass barely moved, which is exactly the point: what shrank is the 28 m column, not the density. So the floor is 2, well under it, because 0-1 is the DEPOSIT collapsing and that is the only thing a density-box read can honestly claim. It is not a look regression detector. check_invariants.py pins the WGSL half and is what stops the two thresholds drifting apart again.
_tickets_about: CHUNK TICKETS (docs/PLAN_chunk_tickets.md §4, src/sim/tickets.h). THRESHOLDS for ticket-settle: the sand poured 40 chunks past the window must be asleep (all 27 active chunks clean in the published snapshot) within ticketSettle.asleepByTickMax ticks of the pour, and the ticket must have released itself within ticketSettle.releaseAfterAsleepMax ticks of that -- kTicketIdleTicks (30) of clean snapshots plus the snapshot latency twice and slack. ticketSettle.ticks is the run's cap. The claims with no number are the ones that matter: the poured mass is IDENTICAL at the pour, settled, read back out of the store, and decoded back by a second ticket; page faults are zero; the run reproduces bit for bit. ticketSettle.hash is an OBSERVATION (the settled box's digest), recorded so a --residency dense run of the gate can be compared against a paged one by eye; it is not compared here.
_ticketLand_about: P2 (docs/PLAN_chunk_tickets.md): ticketLand.maxLatency is the ticks allowed between a stone PARKING outside residency (the first published snapshot that counts it) and its ticket being live. The design value is the fixed snapshot latency (4): the request rides the snapshot of the landing tick and the ticket step of the tick that publishes it activates the box. 8 allows a lost request bucket or two. No number for the claims that matter: two stones in one box open ONE ticket, both are in the store after the release, a request refused at the cap deposits and re-lands exactly once when its chunk is granted, and the run reproduces.
_ticketDecay_about: P3: only DECAY rules run in a ticket. ticketDecay.lifetimeMult bounds when the last of 32 embers must be gone, as a multiple of the ember's AUTHORED mean life (kReactChanceDen / the summed chance of its ungated decay rules, read off the compiled table, so it follows reactions.json and burnDurationPct). 32 independent exponentials: the chance the last one outlives 9 means is 32 e^-9 = 0.4%. ticketDecay.ticks caps the run. No number for the claims that matter: every wood cell under the embers is still wood, no fire appears anywhere in the box (pair and emit rules do not run), some ash is left, the ticket idles out, the run reproduces.
_mobBurnKnown_about: KNOWN-FAILING SINCE 2026-09-04, and the cause is a change the owner asked for. Isolated solids now fall in the CA (soloSolid, sim_step.wgsl) -- and EMBER is a solid, so a lone ember drops and carries fire downward. The owner was asked directly whether hot materials should be excluded and chose to keep them falling. Two of this gate's subchecks measure that directly: 'heat across a joint' isolates cross-limb conduction by setting crossLimbPct to 0, and the thigh now takes 94/558 voxels at that setting against 0/558 before, because heat is arriving by falling onto it rather than through the joint; 'cloth vs flesh' wants cloth to burn faster than skin and now sees skin 96% consumed against 45%. ATTRIBUTED, not assumed: the same binary with the rule disabled passes both (thigh 0/558, skin 45%), measured at gate scope on both arms. This is the fire-down situation again -- a requested change makes a gate red and the honest record is the gate, not a compensating mechanic (the rejected `spark` material, 2026-09-03). _undead_about: Thresholds for the `undead` gate (assets/mobs/zombie.json, MobDef::undead / MobRotDef). undeadLossFracMin/Max bound the fraction of its authored voxels a zombie is missing the instant after Spawn: the floor proves the rot RAN at all (a silently disabled carve would otherwise pass every other claim), the ceiling proves the volume cap is holding. The ceiling is deliberately well above the sidecar's own maxLoss 0.18, because maxLoss is per LIMB and this is the whole body, and because the cap sizes bites from an ESTIMATE of how much of a bite sphere leaves (Mob::RotAtSpawn kRotSphereFill, measured 0.19) -- individual limbs land between 0.5x and 1.7x of it. If this trips, the cap is not holding and a limb is a bad draw away from collapsing at spawn. undeadMaxSpurPerLost is the CHUNKINESS claim, and the only one here that is about SHAPE rather than quantity: voxels left with 4+ open faces, over the human's own baseline roughness, per voxel lost. Speckle strands isolated spurs and a torn chunk does not, so removing the same COUNT as white noise instead of as a correlated blob would leave this number several times higher while every other claim in the gate stayed green. undeadChromaFracMax is the palette filter: the zombie's mean art-palette chroma as a fraction of the human's, which must fall (the gate separately requires luma NOT to fall, so the creature reads as pale rather than merely dirty). undeadWoundFracMin/undeadStainFracMin are the BLOOD claim, and they are two numbers because the soak is two different mechanisms and a regression that killed one would hide behind the other: the REWRITE turns exposed tissue into the wound MATERIAL (the red in the hole) and the SMEAR lays a stain OVER what the hole exposed, bone included, which the rewrite refuses on purpose. Floors rather than bands, as fractions of the body so they do not drift with the art resolution, and each is checked against the living control arm: an unrotted human must have ZERO of both, or there-is-blood-on-it is not a result -- EXCEPT for the rewrite, where the control arm is deliberately NOT zero: a living human already contains blood voxels, because its anatomy speckles the muscle layer with blood at fraction 0.06 (182 of 26,494 measured). So the rewrite is tested as a RATIO, undeadWoundOverAnatomy, against that baseline, while the smear -- which only damage ever applies -- is tested against a true zero. The first version of this gate asserted the human had no blood at all and failed, correctly, because the claim was wrong rather than the feature. Setting rot.stainScale to 0 in the sidecar takes both to zero. Both floors sit lower than the numbers they guard BY DESIGN since 2026-09-15, because half the holes are now dry on purpose (rot.dryFraction): measured 0.029 and 0.137 against the all-wet 0.095 and 0.290. undeadDryWallFracMin/Max are the OTHER end of that spectrum, and the claim the floors above cannot make: of the tissue showing through the holes -- an EXPOSED voxel whose material the INTACT body never shows, that set being measured off the living control arm rather than hardcoded so an art edit or a material rename cannot break it, minus anything already rewritten to the wound material -- what share carries NO stain at all. A BAND and not a floor, because either end alone is satisfied by a uniform: all-dry is the bloodless rot this replaced and all-wet is what replaced it, and the point of the feature is that it is neither. Guarded against vacuity by requiring at least 200 wall voxels, so '0 of 0 are clean' cannot pass on a division. Measured 0.378 on 2026-09-15. FLOOR LOWERED 0.20 -> 0.05 on 2026-09-19 for the owner's gore retune: the smear's reach is stainCutRadius / woundStainRadius times the rewrite's (Mob::StainWoundAs tintRatio), and that ratio went from 1.6/0.9 = 1.8 to 0.4/0.1 = 4.0, so the wet half of the holes now bleeds across the dry half -- same rot, same dryFraction 0.5, measured 0.110 clean walls. 0.05 sits at half of that and still fails the all-wet uniform (the smear at 4x reach leaves next to nothing clean); if the owner narrows stainCutRadius back toward woundStainRadius the measurement climbs and the old 0.20 floor is the right one again. The intact/dry claims are not rows: both are exact, and since 2026-09-19 the gate prints the count of base limbs with no body after Spawn beside them, because a rot bite that eats a socket USED to reach the joint-attachment rule (Mob::JointRuleApplies was not excluded under inSpawnRot_), and a limb severed at spawn charges gore.severVoxels through DrainBlood -- the only way `dry` can be false in a gate that never ticks, so the two reds always arrived together and the owner saw zombies that spawned dismembered, haemorrhaging and dead (a `vital` limb routes Sever straight to Die). Fixed 2026-09-20: spawn rot is the third inSpawnRot_ exclusion in JointRuleApplies, alongside the bleed and the brain charge, and Mob::RebaseJointCounts re-takes neckAtSpawn/socketAtSpawn once the rot is done so the refusal does not merely move the sever to the first blow that lands near a rotted shoulder. Both numbers stay printed so a return names itself. The gate also records undeadLossFrac, undeadSpurPerLost, undeadChromaFrac, undeadWoundFrac, undeadStainFrac, undeadDryWallFrac, undeadSeveredAtSpawn and undeadBloodLostVox as MEASUREMENTS.
